title: [Chapitre] VIII. Analysis situs (quatrième mouture) : notes manuscrites (26/06-04/07/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: Chapter VIII 'Analysis situs' (1986), part of Grothendieck's programme of a combinatorial, 'tame' topology. The ambient space is a one-dimensional object L, a line or an ordered set. A finite subdivision Δ ⊂ L (a set of vertices, assumed to lie in a class Dvep*(L) or Drap*(L)) cuts L into points and open intervals. A 'préfigure' Φ is a sub-collection of these cells: a set Φ_0 of vertices and a set Φ_1 of open intervals. δΦ = Δ is its underlying subdivision.

The previous page fixes the following data.
- Ψ is an ordered family of open intervals X_i = ]a_i,b_i[ with a_1<b_1<a_2<b_2<...<a_n<b_n. Its 'shadow' is Omb(Ψ_1) (the union of the closed intervals) and Omb°(Ψ_1) is the union of the open intervals. ∂Ψ = {a_i, b_i} is the set of endpoints.
- The finite subdivision Δ contains ∂Ψ. It splits as Δ = Δ_is ⊔ Δ_int ⊔ ∂Ψ, where Δ_int = Δ ∩ Omb°(Ψ_1) are the subdivision points interior to the intervals and Δ_is are the isolated points outside the closed intervals.
- A subset Δ_loc ⊂ Δ_int is chosen, and Δ_red = Δ_int \ Δ_loc.
- A subset ∂_0 ⊂ ∂Ψ of 'proper' boundary vertices is chosen.
- Φ_0 = ∂_0 ∪ Δ_red ∪ Δ_is, and Φ_1 is the set of interstitial intervals of Δ contained in Omb(Ψ).

This page records the invariants of the resulting préfigure:
- δΦ = Δ;
- ∂Φ = ∂Ψ, with ∂_0Φ = ∂_0 and ∂_impΦ = ∂Ψ \ ∂_0;
- Φ_is = Δ_is, Φ_red = Δ_red, Φ_loc = Δ_loc.

It then states that every préfigure arises in exactly one way from these data:
- Ψ, i.e. a chain X_1 <_1 ... <_1 X_n, i.e. a_1<b_1<...<a_n<b_n;
- ∂_0 ⊂ ∂Ψ ⊂ Δ with Δ ∈ Dvep*(L);
- Δ_loc ⊂ Δ ∩ Omb°(Ψ_1), which equals Omb(Ψ_1) ∩ (Δ \ ∂Ψ).

Φ is irredundant iff Δ_red = ∅, i.e. iff Δ_loc = Δ ∩ Omb°(Ψ_1). Here Omb°(Ψ) is the union of the Omb°(Ψ_i). In words: no subdivision vertex lying inside one of the chosen intervals is kept as a vertex of Φ.

Corollary: giving an irredundant préfigure is equivalent to giving Ψ together with ∂_0 ⊂ ∂Ψ ⊂ Δ, Δ ∈ Dvep*(L).

Purpose: a combinatorial parametrisation of the 'figures' (finite unions of points and open intervals, with a chosen subdivision) on a 1-dimensional tame space. This is the base case of a cell-decomposition theory for tame/semi-linear spaces. The next page judges the presentation 'franchement compliqué' and replaces it with the direct description Φ = (Δ, Φ_1 ⊂ intervals of Δ, Φ_0 ⊂ Δ).
errors: The text says 'Toutes figures' but means préfigures. It also cites data 1°)–4°) although the previous page only numbers 1°) and 2°) explicitly; Ψ and Δ are the implicit other two.
'Ψ_1' denotes the set of 1-cells (intervals) of Ψ, not the first interval. The notation is easy to misread but the mathematics is consistent.

The bijection claim is correct as long as Φ_1 is required to consist exactly of the Δ-intervals inside Omb(Ψ), and Ψ's intervals are separated (a_{i+1} > b_i strictly). Under these hypotheses no gap is visible. Grothendieck himself abandons this presentation on the next page as overcomplicated.

ideas.what: Encoding a finite union of points and open intervals of a line, with a subdivision, by (intervals Ψ, boundary vertices kept, subdivision Δ, redundant interior vertices)
ideas.modern_name: combinatorial description of subcomplexes / constructible subsets of a 1-dimensional cell decomposition (o-minimal cell decomposition in dimension 1)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard; o-minimal cell decomposition: van den Dries, Knight–Pillay–Steinhorn (1980s)
ideas.where_published: tame topology programme only sketched in Esquisse d'un programme (1984), §5

ideas.what: Notion of irredundant préfigure (no superfluous vertices inside intervals) and the bijection irredundant préfigures ↔ (Ψ, ∂_0 ⊂ ∂Ψ ⊂ Δ)
ideas.modern_name: minimal/coarsest stratification; removing redundant vertices of a 1-dim CW structure

deep.surprise_reason: This is an elementary bookkeeping page in the 1-dimensional case of Grothendieck's unpublished 'analysis situs' (tame topology). The combinatorics is routine, and Grothendieck himself discards the presentation on the next page. It is of documentary interest only, as a trace of the tame-topology project.
transcription_corrections: The relation between the X_i is written '<_1' (strict order relation on intervals: X_1 <_1 X_2 <_1 ...), not '⊂·'.
'Dvep*(L)' is uncertain in the image. The next page has 'Drap^L(L)'; it may be the same symbol (Drap* or Dvp*), so the reading is ambiguous.
The struck-out line under ∂_0 ⊂ ∂Ψ ⊂ Δ reads roughly '∆_{...} ⊂ Δ_loc ⊂ Omb°(Ψ_1)' followed by '= (Δ \ ∂Ψ) ∩ Omb(Ψ_1)'. A small 'U / Δ_loc' is written under Δ, indicating Δ_loc ⊂ Δ.
In the irredundancy line the parenthetical reads '(où Omb°(Ψ) = ⋃_{1≤i≤n} Omb°(Ψ_i))', followed by a marginal '(nommer disparaît)' or similar; it is barely legible.
